title: Frame30 Universal Verification Mould (DICE) Stage 2.4: External Verification Authority & Trust-Boundary Enforcement
objective: Establish an external verification launcher and independent execution boundary such that the candidate repository no longer controls the verification authority evaluating that candidate. Remove all candidate-local trust fallbacks in root-of-trust, validate trusted root identity against approved baseline commit/tree, hash all authoritative inputs in policy manifest, isolate attestation signing authority into a separately controlled service requiring 7-point independent qualification re-verification, eliminate all string-interpolated shell command execution, execute mandatory checks using trusted verifier binaries against candidate source, implement structured command profiles and multi-oracle evaluation, and verify resilience via a 14-scenario adversarial candidate mutation test suite.
merchant_or_user_outcome: Guarantees cryptographic and operational certainty that candidate changes cannot weaken or subvert the verification authority evaluating them, ensuring absolute build integrity and eliminating false passes across all releases.
problem_and_evidence: In Stage 2.3, several circular-trust vulnerabilities remained: (1) candidate repository executed its own local scripts/dice-bootstrap.mjs as the launcher, allowing malicious candidates to bypass harness evaluation, (2) getTrustedPath() fell back to candidate repo on cache miss and seeded trusted-keys.json from candidate storage, (3) DICE_SIGNING_KEY was exposed to candidate execution process rather than isolated to a downstream verifier, (4) shell-interpolated execSync calls created shell command injection risks, (5) mandatory obligations executed candidate-local scripts inside the sandbox rather than trusted verifier distribution binaries, (6) adapter profiles lacked structured arguments and non-multi_assert oracles lacked evaluation engines.
behavioral_requirements: 1. External verification launcher: Candidate repo does not control harness invocation; authoritative launcher executes pinned verifier distribution outside candidate checkout.
2. Zero local trust fallbacks: getTrustedPath() and trusted-keys fail closed as BLOCKED on cache miss; zero fallback to candidate repo.

3. Pinned root authentication: Trusted root validates approved commit (2d1d32f9b49628ce0a4ae8ff9cbe805e94cb4271) and tree (f8932f94a9179feea432073105739ed3c2fac294); policy manifest hashes all authoritative inputs.
4. Signing authority isolation: Candidate qualification process never receives DICE_SIGNING_KEY; standalone signing service independently verifies 7 gates before issuing DSSE attestation.
5. Zero shell interpolation: All git, archive, and filesystem invocations use structured argument vectors and strict SHA/ref/path validation; hostile shell inputs fail closed without execution.
6. Genuine trusted mandatory verification: Mandatory checks execute trusted verifier binaries mounted at /workspace/trusted; candidate code is strictly subject of inspection.
7. Multi-oracle evaluation & structured adapter profiles: Profiles use structured executables and arguments; evaluators explicitly evaluate multi_assert, exact_match, and kernel_verdict.
8. 14-scenario adversarial candidate mutation matrix: Proves that candidate tampering across all 12 key surfaces, signer-key theft, and hostile injection are detected and blocked.
forbidden_behaviors: 1. Executing authoritative verification launcher from candidate scripts directory.
2. Falling back to candidate checkout for missing trusted assets, policies, or signing keys.
3. Exposing DICE_SIGNING_KEY to the candidate execution process.
4. Using shell string interpolation in execSync or passing unsanitized contract inputs to shell.
5. Executing candidate-local copies of mandatory verifiers as the verification oracle.
